newsitem.title: SAO TOME AND PRINCIPE: World Bank warns Sao Tome to regularise debt.
newsitem.headline: World Bank warns Sao Tome to regularise debt.

text.p: The World Bank has warned the African state of Sao Tome and Principe that it must take immediate steps to regularise its $300 million foreign debt or it may lose facilities to renegotiate the debt, officials said.
They said a letter sent by the World Bank to President Miguel Trovoada said that the government must show evidence that it was cutting state spending and fighting poverty.
"The authorities of the country must begin indispensable preparations to prepare the budget for fiscal year 1998," the officials quoted the letter as saying.
Sao Tome's public finances and inflation rate have deteriorated in recent months as it grappled with a series of strikes by health workers, teachers and civil servants.
The former Portuguese colony, located 200 km (125 miles) off Gabon, is one of the poorest countries in the world and is heavily dependent on foreign aid. The islands' population is 127,000.
